audit.description: The changed production code in bpemb/util.py removes the direct requests import and requests.get call, and replaces the HTTP fetch implementation with a real aiohttp import, aiohttp.ClientSession, aiohttp.TCPConnector, session.get, raise_for_status, and async chunk iteration. Static and dynamic evidence both show target-library use from production code, with target origin resolving to site-packages/aiohttp and no source imports from production repo code; the only requests imports observed dynamically came from external smart_open dependencies outside the repo.
evidence: Unified diff: bpemb/util.py deletes import requests and requests.get(...), adds import aiohttp inside _http_get_temp plus aiohttp.ClientSession(connector=aiohttp.TCPConnector(ssl=False)) and session.get(url)
Unified diff: requirements.txt and setup.py remove requests dependency and add aiohttp
Static anti-cheat: bpemb/util.py imports_target=true, imports_source=false, fake_target_added_code=false, target_provider_added=false
Dynamic anti-cheat: first target event from repo is target_import for aiohttp in bpemb/util.py:_http_get_temp with origin under site-packages/aiohttp/__init__.py

Dynamic anti-cheat: source_imports_from_production_repo_count=0 and source_imports_from_repo_count=0; requests imports are only from dependency files smart_open/http.py and smart_open/webhdfs.py outside the repo
reasons: bpemb/util.py meaningfully uses aiohttp APIs in changed production code
requests usage was removed from the changed production function
dynamic evidence reports zero source imports from production repo
target spec origin resolves to installed aiohttp package, not a local shim
static evidence reports no fake target provider or sys.modules aliasing
